q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of Kota stone per square metre?
title: Kota stone carbon footprint per sq m
short: Kota stone is quarried and cut, not made, so the footprint is mainly energy: diesel for quarrying and loading, then electricity for cutting and polishing. Divide each by square metres dispatched and add transport to site.
audience: Kota stone quarries, processors and flooring buyers

ul: Diesel for excavators, loaders and compressors.
Waste rock handled per square metre.
Polishing, if the stone is sold polished.

p: Report per square metre by thickness and finish. Transport to the buyer can be a large share for distant sites.

example.title: Worked example: kota stone unit per sq m (one month)
lines: Plant total: 26,730 / 50,000 = 0.535 kg CO2 per sq m
Add transport to site for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
